decided.question: does this spec add `ViewTimeOffCalendar` to `Capability` alone, or to both unions with a lowercase-dashed twin, and which helper does the calendar's gate call
decided.chose: both unions ship — `ViewTimeOffCalendar` in `Capability`/`ROLE_CAPABILITIES` and `view-time-off-calendar` in `MemberCapability`/`CAPABILITY_MATRIX`, granted to admin, manager and user in each and `false` for viewer in the matrix — and the calendar's own gate reads the twin through `can(role, 'view-time-off-calendar')`
decided.rejected: adding it to `Capability` alone and checking it with `hasCapability`
decided.why: rule 2 — the shipped gate beside it in the same nav group is `can(caller.role, 'view-holidays')` in `HolidaysService`, and every capability the surrounding specs added for a service check ships in both spellings; `Capability` alone would spell this one gate differently from its neighbour. The Shared code table now names the right file for each spelling (`MemberCapability` and `CAPABILITY_MATRIX` are in `packages/validation/src/index.ts`, not `roles.ts`), and the false claim 'matching every capability that came before it' is gone
decided.recordedAt: specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md §Roles & Permission Matrix, the Decided paragraph under the opening prose; carried into the contracts' Routes table, its Shared code rows, and README's Blast Radius and Backward Compatibility 4

decided.question: is REQ-01-007's `none` sentinel reachable from the screen, or is the unassigned bucket API-only
decided.chose: the screen reaches it: `calendar-teams-picker` lists an **Unassigned** entry above the projects which submits `projectIds=none`, it ticks and unticks like a project, and it may be the only entry ticked
decided.rejected: declaring the bucket API-only and rewriting edge case 6's 'ticks' into a query string
decided.why: rule 1 — the spec already answers this twice in its own text: TC-01-INT-04's first read is `projectIds=none` alone and expects `200` with one row, and edge case 6 has a reader ticking it. API-only would have had to delete both. No new testid: the entry lives inside the picker the id table already declares

decided.question: is `days[].weekday` ISO 1–7 or JavaScript 0–6
decided.chose: the field is dropped from the payload
decided.why: rule 1 of repair by subtraction — no requirement, case or edge case reads `weekday`; `date` and `isWeekend` carry every rule the spec states, and the weekend rule is REQ-01-032's. Deleting the field is the repair that cannot be got wrong; pinning it would have kept a value nothing asserts

decided.question: which status does `PUT .../members/{memberId}` answer for an invalid `countryCode`, when its own fields answer 400 and the spec asked for 422
decided.chose: `400` carrying `HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid` on the member write (REQ-01-051), and `422` carrying the same message on the organization country write (REQ-01-036)
decided.rejected: `422` on both, which the routes table and REQ-01-036 previously said
decided.why: rule 1 — the shipped route refuses an invalid role and an invalid job title with `BadRequestException`, and the contracts' own note says one route does not get two refusal shapes because a field was added to it. One form refusing one of its fields in a second status is a client branching per field; the message a caller reads is identical either way
decided.recordedAt: REQ-01-036 and the new REQ-01-051 with their shared Decided; the Routes table row, the refusal-shape paragraph under it, and the note under the Validation Rules table; observed by TC-01-INT-25, which now submits `pl` and expects the 400

decided.question: does a restored membership keep the country stated on it, or lose it the way it loses its job title
decided.chose: it keeps it — REQ-01-048: when a `removed` membership becomes `active` again, `Membership.countryCode` is left at the value stored on it
decided.rejected: clearing it with the job title
decided.why: rule 3 — clearing it pays a returning member global holidays only until somebody notices, which is a silent change to what Amounts Owed pays; keeping it changes nothing about the member and is visible on the detail screen. A country is a payroll fact about the person, not about the posting they left
decided.recordedAt: REQ-01-048 and its Decided, in §The countries, and who states them; observed by the new TC-01-INT-28
